title: Data Cloud grounding and retrieval concepts
objectives: Explain grounding and retrieval so generative answers come from allowed company data, not the model alone.
Use Data 360 as the current Help name for the platform formerly called Data Cloud, without dropping the curriculum phrase.
Map Agentforce Data Library pieces: source, chunks, search index, retriever, and Ready status.
Distinguish packaged Data Library RAG from Service AI Grounding and from uncited custom retrievers.
diagnostic_question: An agent invents a 90-day return window that is not in Knowledge. Before reading, what is grounding, what is retrieval, what must be Ready, and how does Data 360 (formerly Data Cloud) participate?
definition: Grounding means the generative response is based on a defined data source. Retrieval augmented generation (RAG) searches, retrieves, and inserts relevant chunks into the prompt. Help now calls the data platform Data 360; as of 14 October 2025 Data Cloud was rebranded to Data 360 with unchanged functionality during the transition. Agentforce Data Library packages a vector store, search index, and retriever for Knowledge or files. ([Get to Know Agentforce Service Agent](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=service.bots_service_asa_about.htm); [Connect Data](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_data_ingestion.htm); [Ground Einstein Responses with Your Service Data](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.einstein_generative_ai_grounding_setup.htm))
why_it_matters: Without retrieval, the model improvises policy. With a library whose index is not Ready, the Knowledge action fails silently in the user's eyes. Interviewers still say Data Cloud; Help says Data 360. Mixing Service AI Grounding field maps with Agentforce Data Library RAG produces the wrong Setup path.
sixty_second_explanation: Think of an airport baggage claim. Knowledge articles and PDFs are the bags. Chunking is tagging and splitting bags so they fit the belt. The search index is the barcode scanner. The retriever is your claim-check lookup. Grounding is handing the passenger only bags from their flight—not a random suitcase from another airline. Data 360, formerly Data Cloud, is the sorting hub that runs the belt. Ready means the belt is actually moving.
deeper_explanation: Help: use grounding to draft AI responses from a defined data source. Grounding indexes objects and fields so Einstein knows which information to base recommendations on. Service AI Grounding is cited for features such as Case Summaries, Knowledge Creation, Service Planner, and Service Replies for Email, with Knowledge and Case fields. It is not the only grounding path. ([Ground Einstein Responses with Your Service Data](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.einstein_generative_ai_grounding_setup.htm))

ASA Help: with RAG, agents can securely search for, retrieve, and ground responses in Salesforce data. Agentforce Data Library includes a vector data store, search index, and retriever. You can add Knowledge and files from Agent Builder. Fine-tune RAG elements in Data 360 and Einstein Studio. ([Get to Know Agentforce Service Agent](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=service.bots_service_asa_about.htm))

As of 14 October 2025, Data Cloud has been rebranded to Data 360. During the transition you may see Data Cloud in the application and documentation. Functionality and content remain unchanged. ([Connect Data](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_data_ingestion.htm))

Data Library troubleshooting Help: libraries simplify semantic search through chunking and indexing for agents or prompt templates from Knowledge or files (text, HTML, PDF). A library is required configuration for Answer Questions with Knowledge. Prerequisites include Data Cloud/360 enabled and the Data Cloud Architect permission (formerly Data Cloud Admin), Einstein Generative AI, Agentforce, Prompt Builder, and Knowledge if using articles. Saving a library creates UDLO/UDMO configuration, a vector search index, and a retriever (KA_ for Knowledge, File_ for files). Wait until Search Index Status is Ready. ([Agentforce Data Libraries](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=004333412))
The Data Library is metadata. Article bodies and file bytes are business data. Rebuilding an index does not create Knowledge. Exact credit meters and SKUs remain Needs verification.

mental_model.analogy: An airport baggage claim: bags, tags, scanner, claim check, and a belt that must show Ready before anyone collects a suitcase.
useful_mapping: source content (Knowledge or files) → bags to be claimed
chunking → splitting and tagging so the belt can move them
retriever → claim-check lookup that hydrates the prompt
grounding → only bags from your flight, not another airline
Data 360 (formerly Data Cloud) → the sorting hub
index Ready → the belt is actually running
Service AI Grounding → a different terminal for Case/Knowledge field maps on Einstein for Service features
where_it_breaks: A suitcase is physical; chunks are embeddings, which this lesson does not mathematically define.
Help can disable or skip data masking on some agents; that is Trust Layer (AI-005), not the belt.
Custom retrievers and web sources are not supported for some Testing Center generators; do not assume every source type indexes the same way.
The analogy does not encode Data 360 credits.

teach_back_prompt: Explain grounding versus retrieval versus a Ready search index using the baggage-claim mapping, then say why Help's current platform name is Data 360 even though this lesson title still says Data Cloud.

Two-minute interview: retrieval path plus one Needs verification SKU.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: Grounding means answers come from a defined source. RAG retrieves chunks into the prompt. Help's data platform is now Data 360, formerly Data Cloud. Agentforce Data Library packages the vector index and retriever. Wait until the index is Ready.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: I split three paths. Service AI Grounding is a field-map for listed Einstein for Service features. Agentforce Data Library is the packaged RAG kit for agents and prompt templates using Knowledge or files. Fine-tuning lives in Data 360 and Einstein Studio. I never ship FAQ chat with empty retrieval. I mention the Data Cloud name only as the former brand so a 2024 interviewer still follows. SKUs and credits stay Needs verification.

interview_questions.question: Explain Data Cloud grounding and retrieval using current Help names.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Grounding uses a defined source. RAG retrieves chunks into the prompt. Help's platform name is now Data 360, formerly Data Cloud. Agentforce Data Library packages the index and retriever. Wait until Ready.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I keep the curriculum phrase Data Cloud because that is the topic title, then I correct to Data 360 with the 14 October 2025 rebrand. For agents I use a Data Library: Knowledge or files, chunk, vector index, KA_ or File_ retriever. For listed Einstein for Service features I use Service AI Grounding field maps instead. I never demo FAQ before Ready.
interview_questions.example: LAB_ Returns library Ready; FAQ utterance cites 30-day policy.
tradeoffs: Service path vs agent RAG path
follow_ups: What is a retriever ID used for?

interview_questions.question: The agent invents a return window. How do you use retrieval concepts to debug?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: I check whether a Data Library is assigned, whether the Knowledge action is on the FAQ job, whether the article is published, and whether the index is Ready. I do not add a 30-day sentence to instructions first.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Invented policy is a grounding failure until proven otherwise. Help makes the library required for Answer Questions with Knowledge. Identifying fields that are empty or TEXTAREA-heavy can delay Ready. If retrieval returns nothing, instructions should escalate rather than guess. Sharing and Trust Layer can still hide articles; that is AI-005, but I start with Ready and assignment.
interview_questions.example: Index still building; tester ran FAQ two minutes after Save.
tradeoffs: Wait for Ready vs demo pressure
follow_ups: What if identifying fields match another library?
weak_answer_warnings: Granting Modify All Data to fix RAG

interview_questions.question: When do you choose Service AI Grounding versus an Agentforce Data Library?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: If the feature is on the Service AI Grounding table—Case Summaries, Knowledge Creation, Service Planner, Service Replies—use that field map. If an agent or prompt template needs Knowledge/file RAG, use a Data Library.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Help is explicit that Service AI Grounding is for listed Einstein for Service features and that other AI features have their own options. I will not 'turn on grounding' as a single org-wide switch and expect ASA FAQ to work. Conversely, a Data Library does not automatically ground Case Summaries. I cite the table in the design review.
interview_questions.example: Case Summaries use Case fields and feed; ASA FAQ uses LAB_ Knowledge library.
tradeoffs: Two Setup paths vs one slogan
follow_ups: What objects does Case Summaries use?
Can both exist in one org?

interview_questions.question: What happens when you save a new Knowledge Data Library?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Background processes create UDLO and UDMO configuration, a vector search index, and a retriever. You wait until the index is Ready. Retrievers are named KA_ for Knowledge.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I do not pretend to know undocumented object internals beyond Help. I do know the operational gates: Data Cloud/360 plus Data Cloud Architect, Einstein Generative AI, Agentforce, Prompt Builder, Knowledge if used. Same identifying fields can reuse an index. TEXTAREA identifying fields can slow Ready. Then I assign the library to the agent.
interview_questions.example: LAB_FAQ library; KA_LAB_FAQ retriever; status Ready the next morning.
tradeoffs: Reuse index vs isolate identifying fields
weak_answer_warnings: Inventing undocumented object APIs as interview trivia

interview_questions.question: A VP says we already have Data Cloud so grounding is done. Respond.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Data 360 being enabled is a prerequisite, not a finished RAG design. You still choose Data Library versus Service AI Grounding, pick sources, wait for Ready, and assign the library or field map.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I congratulate them on the platform, then I draw the baggage-claim map. A sorting hub without bags, tags, or a running belt does not return luggage. I also correct the name to Data 360. Credits and SKUs stay Needs verification. I ask which feature they think is grounded—Case Summaries or ASA FAQ—because Help splits those paths.
interview_questions.example: Org has Data 360; no Data Library; ASA still invents warranty text.
follow_ups: What permission is required to set up libraries?
weak_answer_warnings: Agreeing that the SKU equals grounding

interview_questions.question: How do you Rebuild a Data Library index without sounding reckless?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Help documents Rebuild on the Search Index, which indexes the library from scratch. I treat it as a maintenance action with an owner, not a panic button in production.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I confirm I am on the correct KA_ or FileUDMO_SI index. I check Refresh History and UDMO Ready first. Rebuild is for when chunks are stale or troubleshooting directs it. I do not rebuild production during peak chat without a window. After Rebuild I wait for Ready again before testing.

interview_questions.question: Where do prompt templates meet retrievers?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Answer Questions with Knowledge uses a prompt template that dynamically uses retriever IDs to fetch chunks and hydrate the prompt. Custom templates can use the same idea.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: AI-003 owns template types; this lesson owns the retrieval side. The template is metadata. The chunks are data. If the retriever ID is wrong or the index is not Ready, the best prompt in Prompt Builder still hallucinates. I do not stuff the article into the template body.

interview_questions.question: Defend not grounding a demo agent at all.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: I would not. An ungrounded demo teaches stakeholders that invented policy is acceptable. If we lack Knowledge, I scope the demo to a scripted escalate path, not fake FAQs.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Help's whole RAG story exists because LLMs invent. A kitchen with no pantry still talks. I would rather show three sourced answers and one honest escalate than twenty fluent lies. If Data 360 is not licensed, I mark Needs verification and I do not pretend retrieval works. That is also how I protect Trust and later testing topics.
